189798c9f9af:
Buses = (journey + layover) × 2 ÷ headway = (25 + 5) × 2 ÷ 10 = 60 ÷ 10 = 6.

062fe1df470c:
(40 + 5) × 2 = 90 ÷ 12 = 7.5. There is no such thing as half a bus: round up to 8, and the time left over is shared out as 'excess layover'.

9489ace7f590:
Excess layover: the extra time at the terminus so that the full round trip is a multiple of the headway. It is wasted time, which can be reduced by combining routes (interworking).
📍 Book M30 p.4
ce52509fb970:
On a circular route there is only one layover and you do not multiply by 2: (50 + 10) ÷ 15 = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 buses.

bd9d3ac5aa0a:
Frequency = 60 ÷ headway = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 an hour. If the interval divides the hour into equal parts, it is a 'clockface' timetable (easy to remember).

98f31a776407:
Minutes = distance ÷ speed × 60 = 6 ÷ 24 × 60 = 15 minutes.

📍 Book M30 p.8
c3c1a23efc98:

8454510e9f05:
Shifts in the week = 40 routes × 5 days = 200. Minus Saturday and Sunday: 200 − 22 − 8 = 170. Over 5 days: 170 ÷ 5 = 34 a day.

Types of shift: early (from the start of service and the morning peak), middle (starts mid-morning or midday), late (until the end of service) and split (divided in two).

Ways to protect customers' money: a trust fund, insurance of each payment, or a bond with an approved body. Leaving it in the company's normal account protects nothing.

Cards: driver, white; company, yellow; workshop, red; control, blue. All are issued by the RSA.

The driver tells the RSA within 7 days at most, and the RSA must issue the new card within 15 days. In the meantime, they print out at the start and end of each day.

d429a701d7fc:
The company card is used to download the vehicle unit (VU) memory and to lock the company's data ('lock in') and unlock it at the end ('lock out'). It lasts 5 years.
📍 Book M12 p.4

When collecting a hired vehicle, you 'lock in' so that only your company sees your drivers' data; when returning it, you 'lock out'.

When changing driver, the cards must be swapped: the one driving in slot 1; the other in slot 2.

13bab558c0b5:
The tachograph always records in UTC (Greenwich time). In summer Ireland is one hour ahead. France, Germany, the Netherlands and Spain are always one hour ahead of Ireland.
📍 Book M12 p.5
b7cbe86b7692:
It is the chart's speed scale: it must match the tachograph's, otherwise the record is not valid.

21f1a459449b:
If the tachograph is opened, the three styluses leave a mark on the three traces of the chart, and this is visible to whoever checks it.

d798ff402768:
At the start: first name and surname, place and date of starting, registration number and starting km. At the end: place and date of finishing and final km.
📍 Book M12 p.9
4486f7fe1f9c:
The law does not require charts to be numbered; many operators do it for control. What is compulsory: providing enough charts, giving copies if requested, getting them back within 42 days and keeping them for 12 months (2 years if they are used for working time).
📍 Book M12 p.10
63563326dcd0:
If it breaks down on the road, the driver records their activity by hand. It is repaired on return to base; if the vehicle cannot return within a week, it must be repaired on the way.
📍 Book M12 p.11
57b107bfc40c:
Analogue: inspection every 2 years and full calibration every 6, or whenever the seals are broken. The digital one is calibrated every 2 years.

62e8d2899c11:
On the days of that week when they do not drive a vehicle with a tachograph, the driver makes a manual record on a chart so that there are no gaps.

Every week the driver hands in the book; the company checks it, signs it, keeps the copy and gives the book back.

8b9cd9c424e6:
Tall hierarchy: clear responsibilities, close supervision and more promotion. But it is expensive (many levels), communicates poorly from top to bottom and resists change.
📍 Book M8 p.2
f2c51c485026:
The big problem with many levels is that information gets lost going up and down. The other options are disadvantages of the flat hierarchy or are not true.
📍 Book M8 p.2
8a2976e60206:
Flat hierarchy: cheaper and with better vertical communication, but each manager supervises a lot of people, there are few promotions, horizontal communication is worse and it is hard to motivate the base.
📍 Book M8 p.2
67ea3e3af917:
Support staff are drawn as a horizontal branch: they report to a manager (for example, the workshop manager) but have no one under them.
📍 Book M8 p.3
2623d6f48ded:
Matrix: used in projects. Each person reports to their usual manager and to the project manager. Advantage: teams with several points of view. Risk: conflicts between the two managers over staff.
📍 Book M8 p.3
ddbed44928f7:
As each worker has two bosses, they can clash over who uses that person and when.

b5d31a266756:
Total km = 50 × 200,000 = 10 million. Litres = 10,000,000 ÷ 2.5 = 4 million. Cost = 4,000,000 × 1.20 = €4.8 million. Each 1% saving is €48,000.

b4340c75ed7f:
A single KPI says little. You have to choose the key indicators, set targets for them and measure regularly (weekly, monthly and annual reports, charts).
📍 Book M8 p.4
8b39c367a61e:
Benchmarking is used to spot where you are worse than others; if profitability is low, the cause must be investigated and corrected.

The organisation chart shows how staff are organised: jobs, level, who each person reports to, how many each manager supervises and possible promotions.
